Is the issue here that we just need to make upnObjectIdentifier a bytes object instead of a string.  I don't see any utf-8 in that string itself that we would need to encode, just ascii bytes, and python has a decoder for that already if we really want to decode?

Also, if we need an asn1 encoder....

from cryptography.hazmat.backends.openssl.encode_asn1

Seems like it fulfills that purpose without needing a new dependency, right?

Hi Ed, I believe the issue is the need to encode the UPN name using the DER format. For instance, the UPN name malikrafsan@mac1.abc.facebook.com would be represented as b'\x0c!malikrafsan@mac1.abc.facebook.com'.

```
>>> # assuming that upn name is less than 128 long
>>> upn = "malikrafsan@mac1.abc.facebook.com"
>>> bupn = bytes(upn, "utf-8")
>>> values = [12, len(bupn)] # 12 means printable string
>>> header = bytes(values)
>>> data = header + bupn
>>> data
b'\x0c!malikrafsan@mac1.abc.facebook.com'
```

It seems necessary to use the DER format (bytes of types + length + value); otherwise, the cryptography library will throw an exception like this [5].

I suspect that `cryptography.hazmat.backends.openssl.encode_asn1` is not part of the official `pyca/cryptography` library. It appears to originate from this fork [2], which seems to provide the UTF-8 encoding functionality. However, I don't believe this functionality is available in the library we are currently using. I have attempted to search for and utilize existing functionality from the cryptography library, but unfortunately without success. The closest result I obtained is as follows, but it does not produce the expected outcome:

```
>>> x509.Name([x509.NameAttribute(x509.ObjectIdentifier("1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.3"), "malikrafsan@mac1.abc.facebook.com", x509.name._ASN1Type.UTF8String)]).public_bytes()
b'03110/\x06\n+\x06\x01\x04\x01\x827\x14\x02\x03\x0c!malikrafsan@mac1.abc.facebook.com'
```

If we prefer not to import a new library, another approach we might consider is implementing a simple encoding method like this [3] or using the asn1 library [4]. What do you think about it Ed? Thank you!


[1] `pyca/cryptography` related directory: https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/tree/main/src/cryptography/hazmat/backends/openssl
[2] Fork of `pyca/cryptography`: https://github.com/birchmd/cryptography/blob/87b660d5802e22d56a8d17a18bdadfc1082739fd/src/cryptography/hazmat/backends/openssl/encode_asn1.py#L59
